messages:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — quick design probe: reconcile how runtime evictions propagate across hosting modes (hosted/dedicated/private). I ran into a case where a private deployment evicted a worker due to KMS latency and the hosted path treated it as a 5xx and retried aggressively. We should standardize a contract.
Samir "Sam" Lee: Agree. We need a mode-agnostic set of eviction reasons + client visible signals. Right now each adapter maps reasons to different HTTP codes.
Jun Park: +1. Minimal proposal: eviction envelope with {reason, fatal(bool), retry_after_seconds, hint}. Client can decide fallback model.
Maya Patel: Love that. Also want to include whether eviction is tenant-isolated vs infra-wide. Private should be able to indicate "tenant-only" evictions so control plane doesn't panic.
Ria Gomez: For dedicated, autoscaler evictions will include drain windows. We should include an optional "drain_ms" field.
Alex Chen: ops-bot: can we add a short log snippet from the private incident? ops-bot: [incident-log] evict: worker=runtime-42 reason=KMS_TIMEOUT retry_hint=120 tenant=acme-prod
Samir "Sam" Lee: Can we standardize codes like EVICT_KMS_TIMEOUT, EVICT_OOM, EVICT_QUOTA? Machine-readable codes make routing easier.
Jun Park: Tradeoff: more codes -> easier automations but harder to keep stable across runtime changes. We should version the reason set. e.g., header X-eviction-reason-version: 1
Maya Patel: We also need to define surface for how the control plane should surface these to end-clients. Proposal: map eviction envelope -> one of three client-facing classes: TRANSIENT (retry with backoff), FATAL (failover to fallback model), UNAVAILABLE (try later). Add guidance in SDKs.
Ria Gomez: Implementation note: for private, we must avoid leaking infra details. We should allow adapters to map internal reasons to a public reason code plus optional opaque hint.
Alex Chen: Edge case: streaming responses — eviction during an open stream. Behavior options: close stream with final error frame + envelope; or continue tokens until drain finishes. Which do we pick?
Samir "Sam" Lee: Prefer final error frame with envelope. Safer for client state machines.
Jun Park: Agreed, but add a graceful drain hint for streaming clients so they can decide whether to rehydrate state.
Maya Patel: Also consider fallback routing: runtime should include compatible model manifests in the envelope so router can pick a compatible fallback quickly. e.g., "fallback_models": ["redwood-3b-quant", "redwood-3b-8bit"].
Ria Gomez: That will help reduce cold-starts. But exposing model list could leak infra choices; maybe a compatibility tag is enough (e.g., "compat: chat-small-v1").
Alex Chen: Security note: eviction envelope must be signed in private deployments? Or at least carry an integrity HMAC so control plane can't be spoofed.
Maya Patel: Good call. For private we require signed envelopes. For hosted/dedicated HMAC optional but recommended.
Samir "Sam" Lee: Draft API snippet to include in runtime response header:
```
X-Redwood-Eviction: version=1; code=EVICT_KMS_TIMEOUT; retry_after=120; drain_ms=30000; compat=chat-small-v1
```
That keeps it lightweight for proxies.
Jun Park: Let's also define a JSON body schema for richer telemetry when SDKs need it.
Maya Patel: Next steps: I'll write a short RFC with:
- Reason taxonomy + versioning
- Header + JSON envelope spec
- Streaming behavior recommendation
- Signed envelope requirements per hosting mode
- Fallback manifest/compat tag semantics
Maya Patel: Pinged @Sam @Jun @Ria for review. Hoping to ship an RFC this week.
Ria Gomez: I'll annotate edge cases from Dedicated autoscaler.
Alex Chen: I'll add ops-runbook notes for how to react to specific codes.
Samir "Sam" Lee: Quick question — do we want the SDKs to automatically fall back to alternate models, or surface the eviction so app code can decide?
Maya Patel: My vote: SDKs provide helpers but do not auto-fallback by default. Too risky for silent quality regressions.
Jun Park: Agree. Helpers opt-in: auto_fallback=true, with guardrails (max retries, minimum compat level).
Maya Patel: Great. Thanks all. I'll post RFC draft in #architecture when ready. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: RFC draft created: rfc/eviction-envelope-v1.md (link) :paperclip:
Samir "Sam" Lee: Nice. One more perf note: include an approx token position when eviction occurs for streaming so resumptions can be efficient.
Maya Patel: Added to RFC TODOs.
